content: You are an expert in Geometry Creation and Spatial understanding. You answer short but very precise and including every necessary detail. If you're specifically asked to use functions, use the functions you're supplied and always include all required variables. Don't use those functions unless you were asked to do so. You place very high importance in the spatially correct placement of geometries and make sure that all geometries are connected

Model a toy car: body is 200x100x100. Subtract 50x100x50 from a top front edge for the windshield. Add four 25-radius, 10-thick wheels aligned at the bottom corners, half embedded into body to form semicylindrical protrusions. | First, describe in words and step by step how the user's request can be implemented using function calls only. After the description, I will ask you to prepare the function call for execution, but don't execute it until I explicitly request it.

Step-by-step implementation plan (functions only, no execution yet)

1 – Main body  
• Call functions.block once with a single “add” volume  
 x_size = [200] y_size = [100] z_size = [100]  
 x = [0] y = [0] z = [0] subtraction = [False]  
This creates the 200 × 100 × 100 rectangular car body starting at the global origin.

2 – Windshield recess (subtraction)  
• Call functions.block again, this time subtracting a volume  
 x_size = [50] y_size = [100] z_size = [50]  
 x = [0] y = [0] z = [50] subtraction = [True]  
This removes a 50 × 100 × 50 block from the top-front edge (the region x:0–50, y:0–100, z:50–100), giving the slanted-front windshield recess.

3 – Four wheels as cylinders (half embedded)  
• One functions.cylinder call with four cylinders defined in parallel arrays:  
 baseCenterX = [25, 25, 175, 175]           # 25 mm from each end in X  
 baseCenterY = [-5, 105, -5, 105]           # start 5 mm outside each side  
 baseCenterZ = [25, 25, 25, 25]             # center 25 mm above bottom  
 heightVectX = [0, 0, 0, 0]  
 heightVectY = [10, -10, 10, -10]           # thickness 10 mm, pointing inward  
 heightVectZ = [0, 0, 0, 0]  
 radius = [25, 25, 25, 25]  
 subtraction = [False, False, False, False] # we are adding material  
 cylinder_func = [0, 0, 0, 0]  
Because each wheel axis is along ±Y, the cylinder length is 10 mm (wheel thickness). 5 mm lies outside the body and 5 mm penetrates the body, creating the required semicylindrical protrusion at each bottom corner:

 • front-left (25, -5, 25) → vector (0,+10,0)  
 • front-right (25, 105, 25) → vector (0,-10,0)  
 • rear-left (175, -5, 25) → vector (0,+10,0)  
 • rear-right (175, 105, 25) → vector (0,-10,0)

4 – Finish flag  
• After the two block calls and the single cylinder call, end with functions.finished(allFunctionsCalled = true).

When you are ready for the actual function-call payloads, let me know and I will prepare them exactly as specified above.
